title: A system of sites compatible up to coherent isomorphism can be replaced by a strict one
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set (a nonempty preordered set in which any two elements have a common upper bound). Suppose given: for each $i\in I$ a site $\mathcal C_i$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] all of whose coverings have finite index sets; for $i\le i'$ a continuous functor $u_{i'i}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_{i'}$ defining a morphism of sites $\mathcal C_{i'}\to\mathcal C_i$, with $u_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$; for $i\le i'\le i''$ a natural isomorphism $\gamma_{i''i'i}:u_{i''i'}\circ u_{i'i}\Rightarrow u_{i''i}$, the identity when $i'=i$ or $i''=i'$, satisfying the cocycle condition $\gamma_{i'''i'i}\circ(\gamma_{i'''i''i'}u_{i'i})=\gamma_{i'''i''i}\circ(u_{i'''i''}\gamma_{i''i'i})$ (as natural transformations $u_{i'''i''}u_{i''i'}u_{i'i}\Rightarrow u_{i'''i}$) for $i\le i'\le i''\le i'''$; a category $\mathcal D$ with functors $v_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D$ and natural isomorphisms $\delta_{i'i}:v_{i'}\circ u_{i'i}\Rightarrow v_i$, $\delta_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, with $\delta_{i''i}\circ(v_{i''}\gamma_{i''i'i})=\delta_{i'i}\circ(\delta_{i''i'}u_{i'i})$. Then there are sites $\mathcal C'_i$ with finite coverings and functors $e_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C'_i$ which are equivalences of categories such that a family of morphisms of $\mathcal C_i$ with common target is a covering if and only if its image under $e_i$ is one, and every covering of $\mathcal C'_i$ is isomorphic (by isomorphisms of the members over an isomorphism of the targets) to the image of a covering of $\mathcal C_i$; continuous functors $u'_{i'i}:\mathcal C'_i\to\mathcal C'_{i'}$ ($i\le i'$) defining morphisms of sites $\mathcal C'_{i'}\to\mathcal C'_i$, with $u'_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $u'_{i''i'}\circ u'_{i'i}=u'_{i''i}$ (equality of functors), and natural isomorphisms $\theta_{i'i}:u'_{i'i}\circ e_i\Rightarrow e_{i'}\circ u_{i'i}$; and functors $v'_i:\mathcal C'_i\to\mathcal D$ with $v'_{i'}\circ u'_{i'i}=v'_i$ and $v'_i\circ e_i=v_i$ (equalities of functors) such that $v'_{i'}\theta_{i'i}=\delta_{i'i}^{-1}$ as natural transformations $v_i=v'_{i'}u'_{i'i}e_i\Rightarrow v'_{i'}e_{i'}u_{i'i}=v_{i'}u_{i'i}$. In particular $(\mathcal C'_i,u'_{i'i})$, indexed by the cofiltered category $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ (one arrow $i'\to i$ for each $i\le i'$), is a system of sites as in Situation 0A34 of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites], and the $v'_i$ induce a functor $V:\varinjlim_i\mathcal C'_i\to\mathcal D$ on the colimit category with $V\circ c_i=v'_i$ for the canonical functors $c_i:\mathcal C'_i\to\varinjlim\mathcal C'_i$. (The construction, Stacks Categories 004A on the fibres: objects of $\mathcal C'_i$ are pairs $(j,V)$ with $j\le i$ and $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$, $\operatorname{Hom}((j,V),(k,W))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_i}(u_{ij}V,u_{ik}W)$ with the composition of $\mathcal C_i$; $u'_{i'i}(j,V)=(j,V)$, $u'_{i'i}(f)=\gamma_{i'ik}(W)\circ u_{i'i}(f)\circ\gamma_{i'ij}(V)^{-1}$; $e_i(V)=(i,V)$, $e_i(f)=f$; $v'_i(j,V)=v_j(V)$, $v'_i(f)=\delta_{ik}(W)\circ v_i(f)\circ\delta_{ij}(V)^{-1}$.)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the categories $\mathcal C'_i$ and the equivalences).* Fix $i$. Let $\mathcal C'_i$ have as objects the pairs $(j,V)$ with $j\le i$ and $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$ (a set: a disjoint union of the sets $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$, $j\le i$), with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C'_i}((j,V),(k,W))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_i}(u_{ij}V,u_{ik}W)$, identities $\mathrm{id}_{u_{ij}V}$ and the composition of $\mathcal C_i$; associativity and the unit laws are those of $\mathcal C_i$, and the morphisms form a set. This is the fibre over $i$ of the category $\mathcal S'$ in the proof of Stacks Categories 004A, the pullback $f^*x$ along $f:i\to j$ in $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ being $u_{ij}x$. Let $p_i:\mathcal C'_i\to\mathcal C_i$, $(j,V)\mapsto u_{ij}V$, $f\mapsto f$: a functor, bijective on each Hom set by definition. Let $e_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C'_i$, $V\mapsto(i,V)$, $f\mapsto f$ (legitimate as $u_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, so $\operatorname{Hom}((i,V),(i,W))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_i}(V,W)$): a functor with $p_i\circ e_i=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C_i}$. For $(j,V)$ let $\varepsilon_{(j,V)}:(j,V)\to(i,u_{ij}V)=e_ip_i(j,V)$ be the element $\mathrm{id}_{u_{ij}V}$ of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_i}(u_{ij}V,u_{ii}u_{ij}V)$; it is an isomorphism (its inverse is the same identity read in the other Hom set), and for $f:(j,V)\to(k,W)$ both $\varepsilon_{(k,W)}\circ f$ and $e_ip_i(f)\circ\varepsilon_{(j,V)}$ are $f$ computed in $\mathcal C_i$, so $\varepsilon:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow e_ip_i$ is a natural isomorphism. Hence $e_i$ is an equivalence with quasi-inverse $p_i$; in particular $e_i$ is fully faithful and every object of $\mathcal C'_i$ is isomorphic to one $e_i(V)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 004A (lemma-fibred-strict, line 7747) and its proof (the category S' of pairs (x, f) with pullbacks g^*(x,f)=(x,f∘g), 'we omit the verifications'), applied to the fibres; the pseudo-functor data and coherence are those of Lemma Tag 02XO (lemma-fibred, line 6420) and Definition Tag 003N (definition-functor-into-2-category, line 5252)

proof.text: *Step 2 (the coverings of $\mathcal C'_i$).* Let $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C'_i)$ be the set of families $\{\varphi_a:X_a\to X\}_{a\in A}$ of morphisms of $\mathcal C'_i$ such that $\{p_i\varphi_a:p_iX_a\to p_iX\}_{a\in A}\in\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C_i)$ (a set: the index sets are those of the set $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C_i)$, and over each covering of $\mathcal C_i$ the families are given by choices of preimages of the objects in the set $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C'_i)$, the morphisms being the same elements of the Hom sets). All index sets are finite. Fibre products: since $p_i$ is surjective on objects ($p_i(i,V)=V$) and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C'_i}(Z,Z')=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_i}(p_iZ,p_iZ')$ with the same composition, a commutative square of $\mathcal C'_i$ is a fibre product square if and only if its image under $p_i$ is one in $\mathcal C_i$ (the universal properties quantify over the same test objects and the same morphisms); and if $P$ with projections is a fibre product of $p_iX_a\to p_iX\leftarrow p_iY$ in $\mathcal C_i$, then $(i,P)$ with the same projections is a fibre product of $X_a\to X\leftarrow Y$ in $\mathcal C'_i$. Axioms of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) (Sites 00VH): (i) if $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal C'_i$ then $p_i\varphi$ is one, so $\{\varphi\}$ is a covering; (ii) $p_i$ preserves composition, so a composite of coverings maps to a composite of coverings of $\mathcal C_i$; (iii) for a covering $\{X_a\to X\}$ and $Y\to X$ the fibre products $X_a\times_XY$ exist in $\mathcal C'_i$ by the above, and $p_i$ maps the family $\{X_a\times_XY\to Y\}$ (for any choice of the fibre products) to a family of base changes of the covering $\{p_iX_a\to p_iX\}$ along $p_iY\to p_iX$, a covering of $\mathcal C_i$ (it is isomorphic over $p_iY$ to the chosen one, and a covering composed with isomorphisms of the members is a covering by (i), (ii)). So $\mathcal C'_i$ is a site with finite coverings. As $p_ie_i=\mathrm{id}$, a family of $\mathcal C_i$ is a covering iff its image under $e_i$ is one. If $\{\varphi_a:X_a\to X\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C'_i$, then $\{p_i\varphi_a\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C_i$ and the isomorphisms $\varepsilon_{X_a}$, $\varepsilon_X$ of step 1 (naturality: $\varepsilon_X\circ\varphi_a=e_ip_i(\varphi_a)\circ\varepsilon_{X_a}$) identify $\{\varphi_a\}$ with its image $e_i\{p_i\varphi_a\}$, by isomorphisms of the members over an isomorphism of the targets. Thus $p_i$ and $e_i$ both preserve and reflect coverings.

proof.text: *Step 3 (the strict functors $u'_{i'i}$).* For $i\le i'$ define $u'_{i'i}:\mathcal C'_i\to\mathcal C'_{i'}$ by $u'_{i'i}(j,V)=(j,V)$ (note $j\le i\le i'$) and, for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_i}(u_{ij}V,u_{ik}W)$, $u'_{i'i}(f)=\gamma_{i'ik}(W)\circ u_{i'i}(f)\circ\gamma_{i'ij}(V)^{-1}\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_{i'}}(u_{i'j}V,u_{i'k}W)$. It is a functor, being the functor $u_{i'i}$ conjugated by the isomorphisms $\gamma_{i'ij}(V)$ (the inner $\gamma$'s cancel in a composite; identities go to identities). $u'_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$: $u_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\gamma_{iij}=\mathrm{id}$ (case $i''=i'$). Strictness, for $i\le i'\le i''$ and $f$ as above: $u'_{i''i'}u'_{i'i}(f)=\gamma_{i''i'k}(W)\circ u_{i''i'}(\gamma_{i'ik}(W))\circ u_{i''i'}u_{i'i}(f)\circ u_{i''i'}(\gamma_{i'ij}(V))^{-1}\circ\gamma_{i''i'j}(V)^{-1}$. The cocycle condition for $k\le i\le i'\le i''$, evaluated at $W$, reads $\gamma_{i''ik}(W)\circ\gamma_{i''i'i}(u_{ik}W)=\gamma_{i''i'k}(W)\circ u_{i''i'}(\gamma_{i'ik}(W))$, and likewise at $V$ for $j\le i\le i'\le i''$. Substituting, $u'_{i''i'}u'_{i'i}(f)=\gamma_{i''ik}(W)\circ\gamma_{i''i'i}(u_{ik}W)\circ u_{i''i'}u_{i'i}(f)\circ\gamma_{i''i'i}(u_{ij}V)^{-1}\circ\gamma_{i''ij}(V)^{-1}$, and naturality of $\gamma_{i''i'i}$ at $f:u_{ij}V\to u_{ik}W$ gives $\gamma_{i''i'i}(u_{ik}W)\circ u_{i''i'}u_{i'i}(f)=u_{i''i}(f)\circ\gamma_{i''i'i}(u_{ij}V)$; hence $u'_{i''i'}u'_{i'i}(f)=\gamma_{i''ik}(W)\circ u_{i''i}(f)\circ\gamma_{i''ij}(V)^{-1}=u'_{i''i}(f)$. On objects both sides are $(j,V)\mapsto(j,V)$. So $u'_{i''i'}\circ u'_{i'i}=u'_{i''i}$ as functors. (This is the identity $g_1^*\circ g_2^*=(g_2\circ g_1)^*$ of the proof of Categories 004A, written out.)

proof.text: *Step 4 (comparison isomorphisms).* (a) For $i\le i'$ and $V\in\mathcal C_i$ let $\theta_{i'i}(V):u'_{i'i}e_i(V)=(i,V)\to(i',u_{i'i}V)=e_{i'}u_{i'i}(V)$ be the element $\mathrm{id}_{u_{i'i}V}$ of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_{i'}}(u_{i'i}V,u_{i'i'}u_{i'i}V)$, an isomorphism of $\mathcal C'_{i'}$. For $f:V\to W$ in $\mathcal C_i$, $u'_{i'i}e_i(f)=\gamma_{i'ii}(W)\circ u_{i'i}(f)\circ\gamma_{i'ii}(V)^{-1}=u_{i'i}(f)$ ($\gamma_{i'ii}=\mathrm{id}$, case $i'=i$ of the indices) and $e_{i'}u_{i'i}(f)=u_{i'i}(f)$, both read in $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_{i'}}(u_{i'i}V,u_{i'i}W)$; so $\theta_{i'i}$ is natural: $\theta_{i'i}:u'_{i'i}\circ e_i\Rightarrow e_{i'}\circ u_{i'i}$ is a natural isomorphism. (b) For $(j,V)\in\mathcal C'_i$, $p_{i'}u'_{i'i}(j,V)=u_{i'j}V$ and $u_{i'i}p_i(j,V)=u_{i'i}u_{ij}V$; by the definition of $u'_{i'i}$ on morphisms, $p_{i'}u'_{i'i}(f)\circ\gamma_{i'ij}(V)=\gamma_{i'ik}(W)\circ u_{i'i}p_i(f)$, so $\gamma_{i'i\bullet}:u_{i'i}\circ p_i\Rightarrow p_{i'}\circ u'_{i'i}$, $(j,V)\mapsto\gamma_{i'ij}(V)$, is a natural isomorphism.

proof.text: *Step 5 (continuity and morphisms of sites).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-morphism-transport] with $\mathcal A=\mathcal C'_i$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal C'_{i'}$, $\mathcal C=\mathcal C_i$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal C_{i'}$, $p=p_i$, $q=p_{i'}$ (equivalences preserving and reflecting coverings, steps 1 and 2), $u=u_{i'i}$ (continuous, defining a morphism of sites $\mathcal C_{i'}\to\mathcal C_i$, by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3)), $u'=u'_{i'i}$ and the natural isomorphism $p_{i'}\circ u'_{i'i}\cong u_{i'i}\circ p_i$ of step 4(b): $u'_{i'i}$ is continuous and defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal C'_{i'}\to\mathcal C'_i$.

proof.text: *Step 6 (the functors $v'_i$).* Define $v'_i:\mathcal C'_i\to\mathcal D$ by $v'_i(j,V)=v_j(V)$ and, for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_i}(u_{ij}V,u_{ik}W)$, $v'_i(f)=\delta_{ik}(W)\circ v_i(f)\circ\delta_{ij}(V)^{-1}:v_jV\to v_kW$ (with $\delta_{ij}(V):v_iu_{ij}V\to v_jV$); a functor, being $v_i\circ p_i$ conjugated by the isomorphisms $\delta_{ij}(V)$. (a) $v'_i\circ e_i=v_i$: on objects $v'_i(i,V)=v_iV$, on morphisms $\delta_{ii}(W)\circ v_i(f)\circ\delta_{ii}(V)^{-1}=v_i(f)$ as $\delta_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$. (b) $v'_{i'}\circ u'_{i'i}=v'_i$ for $i\le i'$: on objects both give $v_jV$; on $f$ as above, $v'_{i'}u'_{i'i}(f)=\delta_{i'k}(W)\circ v_{i'}(\gamma_{i'ik}(W))\circ v_{i'}u_{i'i}(f)\circ v_{i'}(\gamma_{i'ij}(V))^{-1}\circ\delta_{i'j}(V)^{-1}$; the hypothesis on $\delta$ for $k\le i\le i'$ at $W$ gives $\delta_{i'k}(W)\circ v_{i'}(\gamma_{i'ik}(W))=\delta_{ik}(W)\circ\delta_{i'i}(u_{ik}W)$, likewise at $V$, and naturality of $\delta_{i'i}$ at $f$ gives $\delta_{i'i}(u_{ik}W)\circ v_{i'}u_{i'i}(f)=v_i(f)\circ\delta_{i'i}(u_{ij}V)$; so $v'_{i'}u'_{i'i}(f)=\delta_{ik}(W)\circ v_i(f)\circ\delta_{ij}(V)^{-1}=v'_i(f)$. (c) $v'_{i'}(\theta_{i'i}(V))$, for the morphism $\theta_{i'i}(V)=\mathrm{id}_{u_{i'i}V}:(i,V)\to(i',u_{i'i}V)$ of step 4, is $\delta_{i'i'}(u_{i'i}V)\circ v_{i'}(\mathrm{id})\circ\delta_{i'i}(V)^{-1}=\delta_{i'i}(V)^{-1}$, so $v'_{i'}\theta_{i'i}=\delta_{i'i}^{-1}$.

proof.text: *Step 7 (the strict system and the induced functor).* $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ (one arrow $a:i'\to i$ for each $i\le i'$) is a category, cofiltered since $I$ is directed and nonempty and has at most one arrow between two objects. For $a:i'\to i$ put $u_a=u'_{i'i}:\mathcal C'_i\to\mathcal C'_{i'}$, defining the morphism of sites $f_a:\mathcal C'_{i'}\to\mathcal C'_i$ (step 5); for $c=a\circ b$ with $b:i''\to i'$, $u_b\circ u_a=u'_{i''i'}u'_{i'i}=u'_{i''i}=u_c$ (step 3), and $u_{\mathrm{id}_i}=u'_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$; the $\mathcal C'_i$ are sites with finite coverings (step 2). So $(\mathcal C'_i,u'_{i'i})$ is a system as in Situation 0A34 of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites], with colimit category $\mathcal C'=\varinjlim\mathcal C'_i$, $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C')=\varinjlim\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C'_i)$, $\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C')=\varinjlim\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C'_i)$, and canonical functors $c_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-categories](1). By step 6(b) the maps $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C'_i)\to\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal D)$ and $\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C'_i)\to\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal D)$ given by $v'_i$ are compatible with the transition maps, so they induce maps $V$ on $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C')$ and $\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C')$ with $V\circ c_i=v'_i$ (universal property of the colimits of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]). $V$ respects sources, targets, identities and composition: a pair of composable arrows of $\mathcal C'$, resp. an object, comes from a composable pair, resp. an object, of some $\mathcal C'_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-categories](2), where these are respected by the functor $v'_i$, and $c_i$ respects them. So $V:\mathcal C'\to\mathcal D$ is a functor with $V\circ c_i=v'_i$.
